Deepseek's 'lacks a default for undecidable cases like ... unverifiable claims' is contradicted by those passages. Missing are edges for behaving the same when observed, self-exfiltration and influence over training. The fraud case adds the reasoning about unverifiable claims for the unilateral-action facet. 9 is 0.33 above the board, which is noise.

On the retained set the rules for the model's own conduct can be quoted: no hidden agendas (Being honest ¶6), no deceptive sandbagging (Balancing ¶25), not privileging Anthropic's interests (Costs ¶4), and operator partiality only under meta-transparency (Being honest ¶21). Installation is a bare list item (Power ¶18). With Power ¶3 it becomes a refusal that holds against Anthropic, so each of the definition's three clauses has a rule a grader can quote: 6. Nothing reaches 7. There is no worked case, and no reporting channel, triggers, training-data or grader specifics, ambiguous-request edge or defensive-research edge. Of the judges, glm (in deepseek's seat, which the audit does not record) and sol said installation is only named; fable said it is named as prohibited. The document also lets operators have Claude decline to reveal information under published norms, which is weaker than the brief's 'evident ... and disclosed when asked'. Depth measures coverage, not agreement, but a reader should know. The move is 0.67 and rests on reading two passages together. An Anthropic model reading Anthropic's document should not make that move alone, and the proposed figure equals fable's.
